The test image shows two bell peppers with large, dark, sunken lesions covering much of the fruit surface. Key features:
- Dark black/brown coloration
- Concentric ring patterns (target-like)
- Large sunken/collapsed tissue areas
- Affects fruit (not leaves)

This pattern strongly suggests **Anthracnose** — classic dark, sunken, concentric-ring lesions on fruit. Let me confirm with a reference image.

The reference shows Anthracnose spores (Colletotrichum conidia) under microscopy — confirming this is the correct disease class. The macroscopic symptoms in the test image (dark, sunken, concentric-ring lesions on fruit) are the hallmark field presentation of anthracnose on solanaceous crops like pepper and tomato.

No other listed disease produces this specific combination:
- Dark, deeply sunken fruit lesions
- Clear concentric ring banding
- Affecting intact fruit surface
